messages:
maria: quick sync — post-rfc followup. we merged the new routing policy DSL yesterday. need a concise rollout checklist that covers latency vs cost handoffs, region-aware fallbacks, and a smoothing/decay strategy for score volatility. propose a short canary -> regional rollout -> global ramp plan. thoughts?

sam: +1. suggest we do a 3-stage smoothing: instant score -> short EMA (10s) -> long EMA (5m) and route on the long EMA but allow overrides for P95 latency breaches. that reduces flapping on short spikes.

jin: agree on smoothing. one catch: per-tenant overrides. customers can pin `latency_priority:true`. how do we ensure their override doesn't bypass safety (eg. send all traffic to a single region during outage)? we need guardrails.

teo: for guardrails we should add a capacity-aware circuit-breaker in the policy engine: if a target region's available slots < threshold OR error-rate > X, treat it as UNAVAILABLE for routing decisions for Y seconds and failover. also add a max-per-region QPS cap per tenant to avoid hot-shards.

sam: good call. combine that with an admission check in the evaluator: `if region_capacity < tenant_min_throughput then exclude_region`. keep it cheap — simple counters and recent success rate.

maria: let's keep the rollout plan small and actionable. proposed checklist (draft):
• 1) simulation run against 7d production traces (`./policy-sim --replay traces/7d`) : check score delta and route churn.
• 2) small canary (5% traffic) in eu-west only for 24h with `latency_weight=0.7, cost_weight=0.3`.
• 3) enable circuit-breaker + max-per-region caps.
• 4) regional ramp (eu then na) with health gates: P99 latency, token-cost-per-req, error-rate.
• 5) global ramp and enable per-tenant overrides.

jin: add item: telemetry hooks for each decision path — emit `routing.decision.{reason}` with tags (tenant, region, score_components). need this before canary so we can debug.

teo: +1 on telemetry. also add automated rollback trigger: if canary sees >20% increase in 5m error-rate or 30% latency regression on a tracked prompt set, rollback to previous policy version and notify oncall.

sam: small config example for the policy file (for sims):
```
policy_version: v2
weights:
  latency: 0.7
  cost: 0.3
smoothing:
  short_ema_s: 10
  long_ema_s: 300
capacity_guard:
  per_region_qps_cap: 1200
  min_available_slots: 4
```

maria: question about engine boundaries: should the circuit-breaker live in the policy evaluator or be a separate pre-filter service? long-term i'd prefer the evaluator own transient state for locality, but short-term a pre-filter is faster to ship. opinions?

jin: short-term pre-filter (separate service) makes rollout safer and keeps the evaluator pure (deterministic scoring). long-term we can collapse into evaluator if we design a stable state API.

teo: pre-filter also helps private deployments where infra teams want to manage capacity separately. +1 for pre-filter now.

maria: ok let's do pre-filter for v1 rollout. action items: 
• @sam: add smoothing and circuit-breaker sim hooks (ETA 2d)
• @jin: schema + telemetry events (ETA 3d)
• @teo: run canary playbook + rollback thresholds (ETA 1d)
• @maria: update runbook and draft announcement for customers (ETA 2d)

deploy-bot: staged rollout started: canary=eu-west, pct=5, policy=2101234567-v2 (triggered by maria)

maria: thanks all — will post a short summary in #eng-releases when canary completes. :thumbsup:
